title: Throughput Lane SLA & Pricing Experiment for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Define and validate a set of Dedicated Capacity packaging primitives ("Throughput Lanes") + SLA tiers and burst/autoscale primitives so sales + self-serve flows can quickly propose contracts that meet customer's performance, availability, and cost targets without bespoke engineering.
description_2: Hypothesis: Offering standardized throughput lanes (Steady / Surge / Elastic) with clear burst credit mechanics and three SLA tiers (Regional, Global, Platinum) will reduce sales cycle by 25% for enterprise customers and decrease custom pricing requests by 40%.
description_3:
Experiment design (overview):
- Productize three lanes:
  * Steady Lane: reserved GPU commit with fixed throughput guarantees, low burst allowance.
  * Surge Lane: reserved base + pre-allocated burst pool (minutes-based credits) designed for predictable diurnal spikes.
  * Elastic Lane: base commit with autoscale headroom and transparent overage pricing (per-minute billing for burst).
- SLA tiers mapped to lanes:
  * Regional (99.95% uptime, P95 latency target profiled per model family)
  * Global (99.99% uptime with cross-region fallback, lower latency objectives)
  * Platinum (99.995% uptime, dedicated standby capacity and white-glove support)
- Pricing constructs: monthly reserved GPU equivalent, burst-credit bundles (small/medium/large), per-minute overage rates, and negotiated price breaks for multi-region commitments.
- Sales-facing artifacts: pricing calculator, contract clause templates, and a standardized Appendix for SLOs and incident credit computations.
- Self-serve path: include a streamlined sign-up flow to choose lane + burst bundle with clear estimated unit economics illustration in Console onboarding.
description_4:
Metrics / success criteria:
- Primary: reduction in average sales cycle length (demos -> signed contract) by 25% within 3 months of pilot.
- Secondary: 40% reduction in bespoke pricing requests; <5% customer-initiated SLA renegotiations in pilot cohort; acceptance rate of default burst bundles >= 60%.
- Platform metrics: average P95 latency and availability delta vs baseline; autoscale tail latency under Elastic lane under synthetic load profiles.
description_5: Operational / legal considerations: standardized incident credit formula, clear definition of "unavailable" for serverless vs dedicated contexts, audit trail for capacity preemption, and KMS/HSM requirements callouts for Private deployments. Coordinate with Legal for precise contract language and SRE for incident playbooks.
notes: We intentionally separate burst credits (minute-buckets charged up-front) from overage billing (pay-as-you-go) to see which approach customers prefer; hypothesis is that enterprise customers prefer allocated burst pools for budget predictability while dev-first teams prefer pay-as-you-go elasticity.
risks: Complexity in billing engine integration, misalignment of SLA language between Hosted and Dedicated contracts, potential for increased N+1 capacity cost if autoscale headroom is set too conservatively.
rollout_plan: 1) Pilot with three inbound enterprise prospects identified by AE rotation (target: fintech, health, mid-market search SaaS). 2) Internal alpha: enable lanes in staging and validate Datadog dashboards and cost calc. 3) Beta: enable in sandbox for 6 pilot customers for 8 weeks. 4) Evaluate and iterate; finalize contract templates and self-serve UI for public launch.
legal_action_items: Legal to draft Appendix A SLA tables and an incident credit calculator; include explicit KMS/HSM obligations for Private deployment customers; include data residency and audit log retention terms for Platinum tier.
security_qna_todo: Prepare answers for top 10 Security Questionnaire items for Dedicated (network isolation, RBAC, KMS integration, patch cadence, vulnerability disclosure). Coordinate with Security to complete vendor SQ within two weeks of pilot start.
next_steps: Align with SRE on synthetic workload tests by 2026-02-20
Draft price calculator prototype (PM + Analytics) by 2026-02-24
Enable alpha lanes in staging (ENG) by 2026-03-01
